title: finding(plugin-charts): a cartesian chart handed NO series binding at all draws the same silent empty frame #4683 just closed for `series: []`
body:
Measured while implementing #4683; deliberately left outside that card's guard and filed here.

## What is wrong

#4683 gave `AdvancedChartImpl` a refusal for the shape where a series binding was COMPUTED and came out empty — `Array.isArray(series) && series.length === 0`, which is what both `buildChartSeries` consumers (`ObjectChart`, `DatasetWidget`) hand over when a pivot's second dimension was never projected.

The neighbouring shape is `series === undefined`: no binding was ever computed, because the caller never went through `buildChartSeries` and the schema declared no `series` / `categories` / `value` / y-axis fields either. `ChartRenderer` forwards `undefined` unchanged, `AdvancedChartImplInner` defaults it to `[]`, and the cartesian families render `series.map(...)` over nothing — so the author gets axes, grid, tooltip and legend around zero marks and no explanation. That is the same harm #4466 and framework#4033 were filed over, on a third entry path.

Reproduces at the renderer with no dataset involved — render `AdvancedChartImpl` with these props and no `series` prop at all:

```
chartType:  "bar"
data:       [{ status: 'Backlog', est_hours: 12 }]
xAxisKey:   "status"
series:     (omitted entirely)

observed:   no data-chart-error placeholder, no console warning,
            an svg containing 0 marks
```

Pinned as current behaviour by `AdvancedChartImpl.unprojectedSeriesDimension.test.tsx` → `leaves a caller that computed NO series binding at all untouched`, so whoever takes this card should expect to rewrite that test rather than discover a silent contradiction.

## Why it was left out of #4683

Scope, and an honest signal boundary. `[]` and `undefined` are different sentences — "a binding was computed and is empty" versus "nothing ever computed one" — and only the first is the shape that card measured, reproduced and ruled on. Widening the guard to `undefined` changes behaviour for every hand-authored chart that renders with no series binding, which is a decision about the author-facing contract rather than a mechanism fix, so it is filed instead of assumed.

## Worth noting for whoever triages it

The refusal copy #4683 landed deliberately does not name the missing dimension key, because the renderer is not told which dimension the pivot grouped by and two upstream shapes reach it byte-identically (an unprojected second dimension, and a chart with no measure selected both produce `{data:[{status:'Backlog'},...], xAxisKey:'status', series:[]}`). If this card is taken up together with plumbing the pivoted dimension into the renderer, both the `undefined` arm and a key-naming message become reachable at once — see the open question recorded on #4683's PR.

Related: #4683, #4466, #4507, framework#4033.
